note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparisons with A. ctenopher, A. muricatus and A. pectinatus have been given under those species. The alate is distinguished from all the remaining species except A. retifaciens by its rather large compound eyes and ocelli, the two being very close together; A. retifaciens is smaller, with a weakly inflated postclypeus and ocelli closer to the compound eyes. Among the workers, the swollen end of cushion 1 of the enteric valve bears two rows of spines in A. retifaciens, and cushions 2, 3 and 4 have slender hooked spines; A. sentosus is still recognized by the fenestrate base and sclerotized cup of cushion 1; A. spinulatus has more spines on cushion 1 and slender spines on the others; the cushion 1 of A. tranquillus is shorter and incompletely sclerotized.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; pilosity yellow, sparsely scattered. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.30. Mandibular apical tooth rather long, La/Li 0.72–0.74, Ra/Ri 0.96; a deep notch separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence in surface view, La/L1·Lm 11.19–11.50; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are nearly in line, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth slightly longer than that of the second, equal when worn, Ra/Rj·Rm 13.52–15.27. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Tw 5.20–5.64; third apical spur shorter than the other two, reduced or up to nearly half their length. The midgut–hindgut junction is oblique; the enteric valve seat is almost sessile, attached to the second hindgut pouch, dorsolateral in the unopened abdomen; cushion 1 is sclerotized along its whole length, half of it projecting beyond the tips of the spines of the other positions, swollen and bearing 15–23 spines (mean 18.5) on its margin, small spines scattered on the stalk and on the concave surface of the swollen end, the base of the stalk with distinct transverse wrinkles; the cushions of the other positions bear 2–7 slender curved spines (mean 4.3), abruptly tapering, the tips distinctly hooked, with smaller spines over the rest of their length. The valve membrane bears distinct minute spines outside and between the cushions, fringed on small leaflets.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle roughly circular, slightly concave, much smaller than the ocellus, pale yellowish brown; central spot circular, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus paler than the head capsule, iron-chestnut, labrum yellowish brown; frontal groove very indistinct, a flat crescent, concolorous with the postclypeus; antennae yellow. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum brown, transverse sutures almost absent; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae and tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles yellowish brown, sternites yellowish brown, the median part and the ventral spiracles paler; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule slightly undulate, not very evenly rounded; ocelli relatively rather large, their distance from the large compound eyes less than half their minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27–0.28, posterior margin arcuate, not evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.56–0.62, Ra/Ri 0.80–0.92; a distinct notch separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence in surface view, La/L1·Lm 6.88–8.20; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, and the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth is longer than that of the second. Meso- and metanotum rather broad at the constriction, M/W 0.30. Cephalic pilosity yellowish brown, rather long, forming a slightly uneven layer.
